title: A “Black Cat” party
text: A “Black Cat” Halloween party was held by the Academy students at Hindley Hall last Friday evening. Although a little early in the season a splendid time was had.

title: Boys are entitled to fun, but…
text: Thursday evening there may be something doing in town, for that is Hallowe’en. The playful pranks of the boys is not so bad if they do nothing that destroys or causes a pecuniary loss. Boys are entitled to fun, but that don’t mean injury to others. If every boy would ask himself the question before wrecking property: “How would my own parents like to be served that way,” there would be less meanness displayed and more genuine fun resorted to that cost nothing to replace. We wouldn’t give two cents for a boy who couldn’t find enjoyment in 4th of July, Hallowe’en or Christmas time, and have little respect for one whose training has been along selfish lines without regard for his elders or the rights of others.

title: Jokeless Halloween Joke: Unknown Parties Tamper With Teams at a Party
text:
Of all the half witted Halloween pranks that occurred in this vicinity last Thursday night, the worst that has come to light is the work of some unknown parties in tampering with the teams belonging to some of the young people who attended the party at Henry Snell’s in the country.

As the teams were tied outside in the open, the boys deemed it wise to keep pretty good watch of them and went out to see that they were safe just before sitting down to supper at about eleven o’clock. They found everything O.K., then but when they went out afterwards to prepare to go home they found a different state of affairs. The teams were all unhitched and the buggies scattered around everywhere, one of them in a ditch. After a search everything was found except a team and buggy belonging to the Marshall boys, Harold and Sidney. The boys searched until about 5 o’clock a.m., but had to return to town unrewarded for their trouble. After they had been at home a short time, a telephone message came telling them that their property had been seen in the east part of town near Hans Johnson’s home, the team unhitched from the buggy and tied to a tree and there the boys found them. The tongue of the buggy was broken but otherwise there was no damage done and strange as it seems, the would-be-jokers had showed sense enough and heart enough to blanket the team.

title: Received by a ghost
text: Misses Ula and Imo Heebner have been entertaining Miss Helen Hunter of Plattsmouth at their home during the past few days. Among the pleasant events given in her honor was a hallow’een party on last Thursday evening. The guests were received by Master Granville Heebner dressed as a ghost. During the evening various games were played and other interesting and exciting features indulged in, such as some new and novel ways of fortune telling, which caused a great deal of merriment among the young people. Little booklets were given out which directed them to different parts of the house. One of the most ghostly trips was following a string which led them to the cellar where they were received by a ghost who handed them their fortune, which was burned later during the evening. After this, delicious refreshments were served.

title: The biggest dance of the season
text: The Halloween dance at Philpot’s opera house will be the biggest one of the season. Friday night, Oct. 31. —adv.

title: Berlin: the tornado did the upsetting
text: Halloween passed very quietly. The tornado had such a monopoly on “upsetting things” that the boys hardly thought it worth while to try it this year. Henry Junge’s hogs were out the morning after, but the opinion is divided as to whether the boys did the trick or “Heine” forgot to shut the gate.

title: Notice: return the lap robe
text: The party who took my buggy hallowe’en leaving it about four miles east of my place but forgot to leave the laprobe and whip, will kindly return same, as I could make good use of those articles myself. James P. Johnson

title: Extra police on duty
text: The police force was supplied with extra force last night on account of Hallowe’en. Yet a number of traces of the mischievious boys were to be seen early this morning.

title: Drawing witches in the fourth grade
text: Miss Marshall’s fourth grade are drawing witches for their Hallowe’en symbols. Special care has been taken with their writing lessons lately as the best is to be put up in the room, on exhibition.

title: A whole week of pranks
text: …to a considerable extent and carried along until Sunday night, when most of the damage to property was done, which came near getting some one in trouble, as there are not many that believe in keeping up Hallowe’en pranks for a whole week.

title: Correction: not “comical”
text: The type in last week’s Republican made us say in speaking of the Hallowe’en Pranks that “there was enough that was ludicrous in the extreme, without resorting to anything that was comical.” The last word should have been “criminal.”

title: Gladys Philpot Entertains
text: Monday evening Miss Gladys Philpot invited forty of her friends to her home to enjoy Hallowe’en evening with her. They were met at the door with an old lady with a cold clammy hand who greeted and insisted on shaking hands. There were no lights so the guests followed a rope that took them into a room where there was a coon and a clown who entertained them for a while. Then they continued their journey and were led upstairs where two spooky figures greeted them, then on to the cellar where Miss Evelin Doty, dressed as a Gypsy, told their fortunes. They then found themselves in the living room, where they bobbed for apples and played games, sang songs, played the Edison, etc. At this time the refreshments were served, consisting of sandwiches, pickles, doughnuts and coffee, to which each guest helped himself in cafeteria style. After all were served and eaten the boys shelled corn and the girls popped it. The guests came disguised and there were some very pretty and unique costumes. Gladys certainly had a full evening planned and the guests enjoyed it to the full.

title: Hallowe’en Pranks: carried a little too far
text:
The celebration of the Eve of All Saints, or All Hallows, which occurs on October 31st, was carried a little too far by our young people this year. It is unfortunate that we fail to count the cost of our pranks in financial loss and worry, or we think most of the things that are done would not be pulled off. There is so much that is ludicrous in the extreme, and fun is what one is supposed to be looking for on this occasion, without destroying property, which is comical [the next week’s paper corrected this to “criminal”].

Some of our older boys went too far at Mr. Pickrell’s Cream [station] Monday night, and were [hauled] before a justice, Tuesday morning, and given until Wednesday morning 9:30 to repair all damages or pay a fine. If the fine were not paid they were to go to jail.

A younger set enjoyed themselves by breaking off a number of posts in Dr. Fate’s wire fence and laying the fence down on the sidewalk. It wasn’t half as much fun, we imagine, digging post holes and fixing up the fence.

We understand a cap was removed from a hydrant at Bert Reed’s corner which let a stream of water go to waste. This would have been extremely funny if we had had a fire during the night and no water to fight it with.

title: Hallowe’en Pranks: gentlemanly about it
text: The young folks had a good time Hallowe’en night, but were gentlemanly about it. No property destroyed that was reported. Some things moved, and up on telephone poles, etc., but that’s fun and nobody objects, only maybe the fellow who has to get his property home. But it’s in the air on Hallowe’en night and can be expected.

title: Planned a Fine Time
text: The members of the Rebekah lodge had a lively time at their lodge room on Thursday evening. Everybody dressed as ghosts and were put through laughable stunts, which everybody enjoyed. A Hallowe’en program was given. Cider and pumpkin pie were served.

title: A Pretty Window
text: The Halloween window of J. J. Meier’s drug store is very pretty and effective. Hobgoblins, pumpkin lanterns, a profusion of autumn leaves, all add to the pleasing effects of the whole. Lester Rader is the decorator, and he has real talent along the line of window decoration.

title: Led blindfolded through the basement
text: The Hallow’een spirit prevailed at the party Friday night in the high school auditorium. All of the high school was led blindfolded thru the basement, up and down stairs and in the wandering met with various ghostly articles. Games were played in the auditorium and a lunch served. To avoid anyone missing a good time because of spoiling a good suit or dress, the pupils came dressed in hard time style.

title: Alumni Will Have a Big Carnival
text:
To Be Held at the Philpot Hall on Monday Evening, October 31st.

The Weeping Water High School Alumni are the sponsors of a big carnival to be given at the Philpot hall on Hallowe’en evening, Monday, Oct. 31. The alumni members are working hard to provide plenty of amusements and plenty of good things to eat and it looks promising for a big evening for everyone. There will be goblins, ghosts, fortune tellers, fish ponds, museums and booths of every description. A high class vaudeville, with costumes, etc., will be staged, and the usual horns, whistles, and confetti will be in evidence. The “Chamber of Horrors” promises a whole set of new thrills, and in fact, the committees have gotten something new and interesting for every booth. It is a community affair and every man, woman and child is cordially invited to attend.

title: Annual Fun Night For “The Gang” Not Out of Ordinary This Year
text: The evidence of numerous Hallowe’en pranks were visible Tuesday morning, “the morning after the night before.” The windows in most of the business houses were highly decorated with marks of soap, evidence of juvenile pranksters. The Switzer Brothers office was decorated with tires, boards and boxes, perched at rakish angles over the roof. Every year the young people must have their fun on Hallowe’en night, and so long as no material damage or injury to the owners of property is incurred, we think that—well, “boys will be boys,” and we’re all strong for the boys, and girls.

title: Kindergarten: the Leaves Party
text:
At last, the kindergarten children can have their school happenings printed. Sh—Now we will endeavor to tell you of this delay. The children invited their mothers to attend the Hallowe’en party they gave Wednesday afternoon. Laughing Jack o’ Lantern winked to greet them. Each child acted as special host or hostess to his or her mother and friends.

Program: Some went bobbing for apples, and looked for the hidden tiny Jack o’ lanterns. Dick Power found the most and received a Hallowe’en rattle. George Olive gave a recitation, “The Leaves Party,” and the children in leaf costumes then gave a pantomime. Lyle Jewell was the leader for the Brownies. First, he sang a solo, the “Brownies,” and all sang together “Hallowe’en.” John Towle, our big north wind, blew and blew till the leaves all fell from the trees. Bernice Keech, wearing a very clever costume, scattered snow over their heads. Rita Richards could not attend but she sent popcorn balls for all. We had special favors of candy suckers with black mint faces. At least 50 in all were in attendance.

title: Carnival dance at the Dowler Dance Palace
text: A carnival Hallowe’en dance is being arranged for next Thursday night, Oct. 29th, at the Dowler Dance Palace in Weeping Water. Blondy Baughan and his orchestra will be there to offer the season’s latest hits in dance music. There will be plenty of horns, confetti, and doughnuts and coffee will be served free. Come and have a good time.

title: Pumpkin men
text: We made some pumpkin faces Monday. Each had a hat and necktie, making it look like a real man. Some of them were very good.

title: Funniest mask contest
text: Tuesday afternoon we had a Hallowe’en party. Many typical games were played after which we had a Hallowe’en mask contest to see who wore the funniest mask. Prizes for the best masks were awarded: Little folks—Gene Schmader; and for the older pupils to Harold Stander and Earl Wiles (tie). Following this we left the school house and went to a nearby grove where we partook of a Hallowe’en lunch consisting of pumpkin pie and whipped cream, sandwiches, doughnuts and apples.

title: Avoca: the Willing Workers club
text: On Saturday evening Corrine Hallstrom and Francis Druery entertained the Willing Workers club. They celebrated the completion of their first year’s work as an organized Sunday school class. … The evening was very pleasantly spent playing Hallowe’en games and telling stories. Donajean received first prize for having the best costume. Francis received a prize for getting the black cat jig-saw puzzle together. The party was the climax of a successful year’s work.

title: Liberty Theatre: a Hallowe’en Theatre Party for 15¢
text: Mr. and Mrs. Howard Brookings will celebrate their seventh anniversary at the Liberty Theatre on November 7th. … BARGAIN PRICES. Starting Sunday the admission price for “British Agent” will be reduced to 30c. On Wednesday and Thursday of next week, a special anniversary and Hallowe’en bargain price of 15c will be offered on “Murder in the Private Car,” a perfect mystery-comedy for the occasion. Why not get up a Hallowe’en Theatre Party? … Follow the crowd to the Liberty and help celebrate the Anniversary of this important institution and at the same time drive away your cares for a couple of hours.

text: The Saturday night dance at the auditorium postponed to next Thursday, Halloween, when a masquerade dance will be held. King’s orchestra from Omaha. Price 20 and 30 cents.

title: “We have a sure prize for you”
text: Children, when you plan your Halloween party, plan to meet at our store between 7 and 9 o’clock Halloween night. We have a sure prize for you. (From a grocery advertisement featuring Swift’s Premium Ham.)

title: The ghost who kept his secret
text: …Games were played during the evening, and refreshments were served in two courses at tables decorated with orange and black favors and placecards. William Wheatley, who came dressed to represent a ghost, won the prize for keeping his identity secret the longest.

title: Halloween Midnight Show
text: Wef Theatre, Weeping Water. HALLOWEEN MIDNIGHT SHOW. Friday, 11:30 p.m., Oct. 31.

title: Halloween fire
text: A jack-o-lantern caught fire last Saturday evening at the apartment of Mr. and Mrs. J. F. Grow, and set fire to a rug and pair of curtains. The fire destroyed the curtains and left a hole in the rug.
warn: A house fire started by a jack-o-lantern (no one was hurt).

title: Fooling the judges
text: Fooling the judges into believing they were a boy and girl, David and Harold Myers were awarded the $10 prize for the best costumes at the American Legion Halloween dance.

title: Few Halloween Pranks
text: Watchful eyes of the police kept Halloween damage downtown to a minimum, and there were scarcely any soaped windows. Some damage in the residential section was reported. In a pre-Halloween act of vandalism, someone put sugar in the gas tank and crankcase of Henry Friesel’s truck.

title: Eagle: Not Happy
text: Eagle is not especially happy about Halloween this year. Property damages have been reported. Many belongings of citizens, removed as a prank, have never been found. Eagle’s greatest loss is the steel hitching post and chain, an old landmark for many years.

title: A buggy on top of the town hall
text: …the porch lights welcomed excited masqueraders … better than finding a buggy on top of the town hall … or finding somebody else’s livestock in your basement … after hearing about some of the “pranks” pulled in the ’80s and early 1900s, we don’t know what Halloween is all about—thank goodness … modern homes have “upset” lots of plans the past few years…

title: They came as Mr. and Mrs. Harry Truman
text: Mrs. George Smith and Miss Imo Heebner entertained members of their Sunday school classes last Friday evening in the Methodist church basement with a pre-Halloween party. The costumed goblins, witches, ghosts, and other spooks spent the evening playing games. Ramona and Maria Gardner won the prize for the best costume. They came as Mr. and Mrs. Harry Truman. Doughnuts and cider were served as refreshments.

title: Calm Halloween
text: It was a sane Halloween in Avoca this year. Helped, no doubt, by the number of parties which kept the usual pranksters busy. The juniors entertained the high school in the school gymnasium; Mrs. Walter Everman assisted by Mrs. Ellis Lacy entertained their Sunday school classes at the Everman home. Mrs. Albert Sill entertained her Sunday school boys at a dinner Friday evening and then took them to a show in Nebraska City.

title: Costumes to school
text: We are planning a halloween party Oct. 31. In the afternoon we will wear costumes to school. Penny Sue Van Every bro’t a large painted witch to school. Her mother made it for our room.

title: Popcorn balls, Kool Aid and ice cream bars
text: In art, we made Halloween masks. They are very attractive. Thursday evening Phyllis Krogh, Linda Norris, Nila Cooper, Dorothy Potts, Lorine Pointer and Peggy Bender, who were on the refreshment committee for our Halloween party, went to Mrs. Ketelhut’s home and made pop-corn balls. Friday we had the Halloween party. We played games and won prizes. For refreshments we had popcorn balls, Kool Aid and ice cream bars.

title: “Hallooowwweeennn Party”
text: Mrs. Ervin Betts helped Mrs. Arthur Schmidt with a ghostly Halloween party Monday night at the Schmidt home. … They were met at the front door by a very realistic ghost (Mrs. Betts) who made sure they read a sign on the front door. The sign instructed them to follow a rope which led them around the house and to the west door, where they were met by an old witch (Mrs. Schmidt) who directed them through a darkened room on their hands and knees over sheets covering such things as wet sponges, brushes, egg shells, wet noodles, and balloons. Those who survived this ghastly trip were further horrified with gruesome games, spooky rooms and weird noises. On the lighter side, Mrs. LeRoy Stratton was chosen as best dressed woman and Arthur Schmidt won as best dressed man, though he was dressed as a woman. Mr. & Mrs. LeRoy Stratton won a promptness prize.

title: We paraded through the high school
text: On Halloween everyone wore masks and many clever costumes appeared. We paraded through the high school rooms and most of the grades. We enjoyed a visit to the kindergarten room and sang many songs.

title: UNICEF Party Monday Night
text: Monday night at 6:30 p.m. the church bells will ring announcing the hour when the UNICEF spooks and goblins will be out ringing doorbells in every nook and cranny of our town. The 1955 spook will be easily identified. He will wear an orange tag with the UNICEF symbol and bear a milk carton similarly decorated. He will ask you to help him share his Halloween with “all the children of the world” by giving treats of cash. … Each group of youngsters will be accompanied by an adult. … At 8:00 p.m., the children will assemble at the Agricultural Auditorium basement where a gala party has been planned for them, complete with refreshments.

title: Churches Sponsor UNICEF Here
text: A new wrinkle will be added to the time honored “Trick or Treat” program by Weeping Water children this Halloween. In the past the children have gone from house to house gathering loot, such as cookies, candy, fruit, etc., by the bagful. This year instead of requesting treats, the children will be accepting cash donations for UNICEF (United Nations Childrens Fund). The money realized will be used to buy food and medicine for millions of underprivileged children all over the world. The churches of Weeping Water, along with several civic organizations, are sponsoring this movement, the first time it has been tried in Weeping Water. All children will meet at the Agricultural Auditorium at 6:30 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 31. Here they will be divided into teams, given official arm bands and money containers, and will then go forth to completely canvass the town. After the town has been covered the children will report back to the Auditorium where a gala party has been planned for them.

title: Rainbow Girls Costume Party
text: A Rainbow Halloween costume party was held in the dining room of the Congregational church Monday night. All of the costumes were clever and it was hard to choose the best, but by popular vote Jolene Spohn won first prize for the prettiest costume as the “Yellow Rose of Texas.” The Kettles, Pa and Ma, and a friend, Susan Wood, Marlene Noble and Judy Domingo, were judged the funniest. Cleverest was Mary Nichols as the Cavalier. Games and a spook room formed the evening entertainment. Refreshments of fruit Jello, cookies, candies and punch were served.

title: Sandra Baker’s fifth birthday
text: Sandra Baker, daughter of Mr. and Mrs. Lewis Baker, celebrated her fifth birthday on Friday, Oct. 19. A birthday and Halloween party were held in her honor. The 14 guests present came dressed as follows: Pam Saathoff, Patty Wade, Suzanne King, as witches; Heather Stacey, Randy Baker, Stevie Freeman, as ghosts; Carol Wipf, Spanish dancer; Michelle Blecha, Annie Oakley; Timmy Wade, rat; Greg Bickford, clown; Marlin Dennis, Terry Wipf, cowboys; Sandy Baker, a balerina. Paula Freeman joined them after school. Decorations included black and orange streamers, corn stalks, many paper jack-o-lanterns, witches, and cats. A real jack-o-lantern…

title: Hard-Time Costume Dance and Masquerade
text: HALLOWEEN DANCE. Agricultural Auditorium, Weeping Water, Nebr. Friday, Oct. 26, 1956, 9:00 P.M. This will be a Hard-Time Costume Dance and Masquerade. Music by THE STARLITERS. Admission: Couples $1.50; Singles $1.00.

title: Halloween skating party
text: ELMS ROLLER RINK. Halloween Skating Party, Tuesday Night, Oct. 30. Prize For Best Costume. Come With or Without Costume. Regular Admission, 50¢. —adv.

title: Halloween Damage
text: Cass County Sheriff Tom Solomon was called to Avoca Friday morning. Halloween observance had gotten out of hand and serious damage was done to cars and appliances. Rocks were thrown through windows. Much damage was done at the Avoca Oil station where a fire was started.
warn: Vandalism and a fire set at a gas station.

title: $106 Collected For UNICEF
text: Approximately 115 “spooks,” “goblins,” or what-have-you, assembled in the Weeping Water churches at 7:00 p.m. on Halloween evening. They divided into small groups, with adult leaders and began canvassing the town, asking for contributions for UNICEF. They collected money in milk cartons which bore the orange and black UNICEF stickers or tags. These local children have collected $106 at the latest count, which will go to the United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund to provide food and medicine for the world’s children. Through UNICEF, for example, a nickel buys 80 glasses of milk in countries where many children have never tasted milk. … They will see you next year with milk cartons and insignia for another UNICEF Halloween.

title: A Miss America contestant and a clown
text: The Brownies enjoyed a costume Halloween party, Saturday night at the recreation room at the Lewis Baker home. The room was decorated in many mysterious ways with witches, goblins, cats and ghosts. The evening began with a scavenger hunt. … Mrs. Wade’s group won the candy prize. The rest of the evening, the girls enjoyed relays with each group winning two prizes. Then, the girls bobbed for apples. The Brownies voted by secret ballot for the best costume. The vote gave the prizes to Ramona Severn, a Miss America contestant and Joan Domingo, who was a clown. … Each girl was presented a favor of a candy witch.

title: “It’s nice to help little orphans”
text: As my six year old daughter said, “Mom, it’s nice to help little orphans and sick babies, isn’t it?” People ask “How do we know that the money gets there.” Well, we don’t know anymore than we do with polio, red cross or heart fund, it’s just something that we have to believe in with good faith. Let’s all give until it HELPS. —Mrs. Neil Fitzpatrick

title: Around Town: a man hung in effigy
text: …aftermaths of Halloween … a man hung in effigy on the west bridge … identity unknown … much and many soapings of windows and cars … and before Halloween considerable damage at Memorial Field … not a trick or treat affair but vandalism…

title: Youths Draw Fines Saturday Night
text: Terry L. Meisinger, Roy J. Alberts, and Robert P. Wiesneth, all of Louisville, and Frank J. Baker, Cedar Creek, appeared in Police Court Saturday night and drew fines of $50 and $5 costs, each, from Police Judge Gordon Heneger. The four were arrested last Tuesday night, Halloween, and charged with opening fire hydrants, which resulted in almost emptying the city water reservoir. Court was originally set for last Wednesday night, but the four young men failed to appear. Warrants were then drawn up and served by Sheriff Tom Solomon, and court was rescheduled for Saturday night.

title: A flashlight and plenty of endurance
text: Final plans have been made for the UNICEF Halloween celebration. On Wednesday, Oct. 31, you will be greeted at your door by a group of becostumed, weird looking creatures, who appear one night a year. They will be Tricking you, to Treat hungry, sick children of the world, by putting your contribution into their milk carton bearing the orange and black UNICEF sticker. They will be accompanied by a sponsor who wears the UNICEF lapel tag. A friendly reminder—these goblins, like all Halloween folk, thrive on small goodies. All the youngsters of the community are invited to assemble at 6:30 p.m., in the following age groups: Preschool, Kindergarten, 1st and 2nd grades—Christian Church. Third, Fourth and Fifth grades—Methodist Church. Sixth, Seventh and Eighth grades—Congregational Church. Older youth, as well as all adults who can act as sponsors or car drivers for groups are asked to volunteer their services. They will find that it can be fun. A flashlight is of great help, as well as plenty of endurance to keep up with the lively spooks. Pop will be provided by the Chamber of Commerce.

title: Elmwood: discouraging “Candy Tricks or Treats”
text: The Annual UNICEF Halloween Party, sponsored by the churches for all children of the community, kindergarten through sixth grade will be held at the Community Building on Saturday from 6:30–9:00 p.m. There will be fun, games, movies and refreshments. Come and have fun and at the same time you can HELP NEEDY CHILDREN AROUND THE WORLD. … Your UNICEF committee urges you to give treats only to those collecting for UNICEF and to encourage other boys and girls who knock at your door to attend the UNICEF Halloween Party planned for them. Only in this manner can we discourage the house to house “Candy Tricks or Treats” and build our UNICEF program.

title: Costume party at the Legion Club
text: HALLOWEEN Costume Party. Saturday, October 29, 1966. American Legion Club, Weeping Water, Nebraska.

title: The primary parade
text: We enjoyed our Halloween parade in costume and our visitors from the other primary rooms. Treats for our party were furnished by Susan Hunter, Patricia Sudman, Douglas Diltz, Patricia Scott, Jeff Stander, Terry Wilson, Michael Spohr, Renee Wessels, Fonda Mather, David Schreiner, and Mrs. Kivett.

text: Witches, ghosts and all sorts of goblins visited our room Tuesday morning. We enjoyed the parade of all the lower grades celebrating Halloween in costume. We had our Halloween party Tuesday, after the last recess. Treats were passed by Kristine Keckler, Marty Rupp, Denise Mather, Cynthia Stander, Barbara Stocker, Karon Trook, Gail Bruns, Rex Boyd, Kelley Miller, Lou Anne Blaikie, and Mrs. Elliott treated us to ice cream bars.

title: Safety advice for the party
text: For the Halloween party be sure that decorations and costumes are fire-proof or fire-resistant if you plan to use candles or torches. When the trick-or-treat groups come to your door, hand out packaged sweets, rather than homemade foods. By the same token, instruct your children to eat only commercial foods from unbroken packages. Homemade foods and unpackaged foods can be disease carriers.

title: Spook House at the Youth Center
text: One hundred and thirty people and adults were appropriately entertained Halloween evening at Spook House held at the Youth Center. Grade school and Junior High students under the direction of Mrs. John (Peggy) Simons did a fine job in spooking their guests. Next year they plan a bigger and better Spook House.

title: Avoca: Halloween Parade
text: The merchants of Avoca sponsored a Halloween costume parade and party Wednesday night on main street. There was a large group of participants. Judges were Mrs. John Buchholz, Mrs. Junior Lingle, Miss Nancy Dettmer. First prize was awarded to Tessie Dumke, Chris Carsten, second, and there were 10 third prizes awarded. All the children were given treats and adults were served doughnuts and coffee.

title: Invaders Swarm Through Weeping Water Wednesday
text:
Weeping Water was invaded by a horde of goblins, ghosts, witches, animals, etc., of assorted shapes and sizes Wednesday night. The invaders first struck at about 6:30 p.m., when most residents thought they were safe and secure in their homes, enjoying a leisurely dinner, and settling down to an evening of quiet reading, or TV viewing.

Without advance warning, doorbells all over the city began ringing and when the unsuspecting housewife opened her door, she was momentarily stunned by the horrible appearing monstrosities facing her, shouting in childish trebles, “Trick or Treat!” Reacting quickly, Mrs. Housewife offered the invading force some candy, which she just happened to have on hand—luckily the husband hadn’t found this secret cache, or the wife would have been in trouble. This seemed to be the right move, as the monsters helped themselves to the goodies, and disappeared back into the darkness. But this was only the first wave, as almost immediately the doorbell rang again, and the procedure was repeated, over and over again. Shortly after 9:00 p.m., when the supply of loot was almost exhausted, the entire force of scary looking invaders withdrew.

After checking back into the archives, it was found that this invasion seems to be an annual occurence, always coming on the last day of October. Experts in the field have the opinion that these invaders, probably from another planet, exist on candy, gum, fruit, cookies, etc., and these annual forays replenish their stock of food, which evidently lasts them for a year. Using this opinion as a guideline, they feel that Weeping Water is safe from another invasion until Oct. 31, 1974. They caution residents to lay in a supply of the goodies early next year, and not be caught short, as they are not sure what havoc would be wrought if the invaders’ demands were not met.

The Republican feels that these invaders have been infiltrated by some local residents, because one of the early arrivals was questioned as to its identity and the reply was, “I’m a witch, but my name is Angie Wright.” Angie is the lovely little witch in the top photo. The identity of the two in the bottom photo was not learned, as they disappeared before questioning was completed.

title: Avoca: parade, pancakes and a free dance
text: The Avoca merchants sponsored a Halloween Party with a Children’s Parade, a Pancake Feed and a Free Dance with Ernie Emshoff’s Orchestra. Heading the arrangements were Clyde Fletcher, Sr., and Darrell Brinkhoff. Prize winners were Kim Barnhart, Russ Fletcher, Kellie Roades, Doris Sutton and Brian Brockhoff. title: When trick-or-treat changed
text: In about a week, Halloween will be here. Along with all the other things it means, it will mark the time when children dress up in spooky costumes and ring their neighbors’ doorbells. For years it has been traditional to give these annual ghosts and goblins candy and other goodies in response to their gusty cries of “trick or treat.” Yet in the last four or five years, stories have been circulated about people who have tried to harm the children by sticking razor blades in apples, etc. To guard against injuries, many parents have become quite particular about what they let their children eat when they bring their bags of goodies home.
warn: Mentions attempts to harm children with tampered treats.

title: The farmer who moved his outhouse
text:
By Mildred Sadlo. With Halloween time, I am reminded of a story one of my high school teachers told me when I was still in school. It seems the high school boys in this one town would always play pranks on the farmers at Halloween. They had many pranks they loved to do, but their favorite one was tipping outhouses. One old farmer’s really was their favorite one to tip because it really made him angry. It seemed that the more it bothered him, the more fun it was to tip his outhouse.

But one year this old farmer decided he would teach them a lesson that they wouldn’t forget. He moved the outhouse off the holes. Not enough to notice and since the boys didn’t come until he was in bed, they wouldn’t see it. Sure enough! As soon as it was dark and the old man had gone to bed, the boys came to tip the outhouse. They always had to get a running start to do it. The first warning that the outhouse was off the holes came when the first one fell in. … he sank in up to his waist. The others managed to keep from falling in. They pulled their friend out and left in quite a hurry. The car they were driving had a running board and they made the one that fell into the hole stand outside. He didn’t exactly smell like a bouquet of roses. It was a chilly night and by the time they got him home, he was pretty sick. To top it off he had to stay outside until he was cleaned up.

Needless to say, the farmer never had his outhouse pushed over again. In fact, nobody in that town did; the boys gave up their pranks, at least pushing over outhouses.

title: The Halloween “trick of the century”
text:
By Jackie Salberg. It was probably the Halloween “trick of the century” and Mother Nature was the obvious prankster. On Thursday morning, October 31, Weeping Water and area residents woke up to rain, freezing drizzle and dropping temperatures. Due to icy road conditions and an ominous weather forecast, schools were closed for the day. As the day progressed, ice continued to build on trees and power lines until in mid-afternoon, Weeping Water lost its power. The city was fortunate enough to have it restored a few hours later. By nightfall Thursday evening, several inches of slush had built up on streets and highways. Weeping Water city officials decided, for the safety of all, it was best to postpone the annual Halloween trick or treating until Sunday.

Local OPPD office employee Helen Amick spent all of Thursday night in the Weeping Water office taking phone calls from area customers without power. … In spite of sleet and winds growing in velocity, the power remained on in Weeping Water Thursday night, but at 7:15 a.m. Friday morning, the town lost its electricity. The slush of Halloween eve had now turned to ice, snow had started to fall and high winds created blizzard like conditions throughout the morning hours. Schools were again cancelled. …

Business was booming at Meeske Ace Hardware, Hartman’s Family Foods and Rathe’s Variety. Meeske Ace sold out of kerosene heaters, kerosene and propane lamps and flashlight batteries. Linda Rathe of Rathe’s Variety thought she had enough flashlight batteries stocked to take the store to the end of the year. All were sold except four packages. … Hartman’s Family Foods sold out of bread and milk by Friday evening. It was not uncommon to see customers shopping by flashlight. All sales had to be added by hand or with a battery operated calculator. Bernie’s Cafe, Town Tap and the Dairy Sweet were able to feed the people and serve warm coffee as all three establishments have gas stoves.

title: “Dread Haven”
text: The Weeping Water Congregational Church School is once again presenting, for the local public, a Halloween Haunted House. “Dread Haven” is a good clean theatrical scare for the entire family, well maybe not the tiny tots, and is not advertised in Omaha or Lincoln. The wait in line is well worth your time. A concession stand on the grounds will be selling hot chocolate and cookies. Five rooms with guides from start to finish provide 4 nights of entertainment for young and old. Last year over 900 people viewed “Mystery Manor.” Are you going to be a brave soul and try “Dread Haven” this year?
